question: Across the fixed 127 absent ray pairs, do graph novelty, static price movement and root exposure align?
interpretation: On this fixed generated family, every new ray adds some empty-board graph edges and raises its selected type's normalized price. Yet 76/127 have no initial legal candidate; those blockers are occupancy/side-to-move effects, not static-profile rejection. Median normalization also lowers non-selected type prices in 303/508 entries. This is scoped mechanism evidence, not utility or a general price law.
limitations: Eight 6x6 classic-like roots, finite set of absent direct ray type-direction pairs, initial action exposure only; no post-move play, outcomes, search, training, calibration or utility claim.
